title: The hibernatable WebSocket hub accepts clients via state.acceptWebSocket and the wake handler runs from cold reading the same storage
description: A named hub object accepts websocket clients via state.acceptWebSocket per Cloudflare's hibernatable WebSockets shape (https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/), routes each message to per-message handlers by JSON type field, and broadcasts to all connected sockets. On hibernate-and-wake the wake handler runs from a cold start and reads the same storage; the shipped hub class re-emits doWakeUp on the injected event sink on the first message after hibernation. The applying project elicits the broadcast delivery window in milliseconds (do-hub-broadcast-window-ms; recommended default 500): every fan-out from a hub broadcast MUST (must) settle to every connected client, or record a partial delivery on the sink, within the elicited window. The applying project also elicits the hibernate-after-idle window per ADR-3405 (do-hub-hibernate-after-idle-ms; recommended default 30000): every hub instance MUST (must) enter the hibernated state after the elicited idle window elapses with no client activity, and MUST (must) wake from cold on the first post-hibernation message without losing lastBroadcast state. The hub shape realises the hibernatableWebSocket capability token: every consumer that selects hibernatableWebSocket inherits the accept-hibernate-wake cycle this REQ describes.
rationale: Ratified in the Cloudflare round 6 spec (2026-09-06 section 5.3). Ships as v1.0.0 of platform-cloudflare-durable-objects.
